rounds.text: Kross Ltd is materially under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to an intrinsic value of Rs 425 per share against a market price of Rs 287, offering a 32.5% margin of safety [E38, E39]. This mispricing is further underscored by a reverse DCF showing that today’s price implies only 12.6% earnings growth, whereas the base case assumes 18.0% [E40]. The business is executing exceptionally well on top-line and bottom-line expansion, demonstrating a 36% TTM compounded sales growth and a 40% compounded profit growth [E16, E19], alongside a rules-based screening score of 93 out of 100 [E56]. Fundamental efficiency measures remain robust, with ROCE at 16.03% outperforming the sector benchmark of 12.7% [E10], and promoters demonstrating strong ongoing commitment by increasing their holding to 68.57% [E34]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], and free cash flow stands at Rs -72 Cr in Mar 2026 due to intensive capital expenditure [E30] driven by a 243.8% surge in capital work-in-progress [E33].

Conceded: [E14], [E17], [E53]. Despite reported profit growth, a fundamental disconnect has emerged between accounting earnings and actual cash generation [E28]. Cash conversion sits at a weak 0.51x for March 2026, meaning profits are running far ahead of cash collection, which warrants a close check on receivables and accruals [E28]. This cash strain is further highlighted by a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr in March 2026 [E30]. Concurrently, working capital days have bloated significantly from 86.9 days to 124 days [E55]. To fund its aggressive expansion—such as the massive Rs 170 crore seamless tube project—borrowings have more than doubled year-over-year to Rs 119 Cr in September 2026 [E32, E33, E74, E82]. Furthermore, institutional confidence appears to be waning, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropping to 3.37% and 6.10% respectively compared to September 2024 [E35, E36].

While the bear notes a cash conversion of 0.51x [E28] and negative free cash flow [E30], these figures reflect a deliberate capex build-up phase where CWIP has surged 243.8% [E33] to fund a strategic Rs 170 crore expansion [E74]. Conceded: Borrowings have increased to Rs 119 Cr [E32] and working capital days have risen [E55], but the company remains conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of only 0.23x [E31]. Although foreign and domestic institutional holdings have declined [E35, E36], this is countered by promoters increasing their stake to 68.57% [E34] and an overall positive institutional money flow [E37]. The underlying business strength is evidenced by a 150% YoY net profit jump [E59] and a 79% YoY sales increase [E57], which supports a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 425—well above the current market price [E38].

Conceded: promoters increased their stake to 68.57% [E34]. However, dismissing the severe cash disconnect as merely a build-up phase ignores that cash conversion sits at a poor 0.51x [E28] and free cash flow plunged to Rs -72 Cr [E30], driven by working capital days stretching significantly from 86.9 to 124 days [E55]. While the bull points to a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.23x [E31], this obscures the underlying trend where borrowings more than doubled to Rs 119 Cr from Rs 54 Cr [E32] to fuel these capital-heavy projects. Furthermore, citing positive overall institutional money flow [E37] flatly contradicts the tangible retreat of both foreign institutions, down from 5.93% to 3.37% [E35], and domestic institutions, dropping from 9.54% to 6.10% [E36]. Finally, relying on a model-driven DCF intrinsic value of Rs 425 [E38] ignores that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 19% [E50] and that the EV/EBITDA of 16.33x trades at a sharp premium to its sector benchmark of 11.46x [E11].

Conceded: cash conversion is 0.51x [E28], free cash flow is negative at Rs -72 Cr [E30], and working capital days increased from 86.9 to 124 days [E55]. However, this cash outflow and the rise in borrowings to Rs 119 Cr [E32] directly fund a massive +243.8% surge in capital-heavy work-in-progress [E33] for strategic expansions like the INR170 crore seamless tube project [E74], which will drive future growth rather than signal distress. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have receded [E35, E36]; nevertheless, overall institutional money flow is recorded as positive with an increase of 0.91 percentage points [E37], alongside promoter confidence shown by their rising stake to 68.57% [E34]. While the bear highlights an EV/EBITDA premium [E11], the company's operating returns surpass sector benchmarks with an ROA of 9.44% versus 6.48% [E8] and ROCE of 16.03% versus 12.7% [E10], fully justifying a higher valuation multiple given its exceptional top-line growth of 36% in the TTM [E16] and profit growth of 40% [E19].

Conceded: promoter stake increased to 68.57% [E34], and overall institutional money flow shows a slight positive shift of 0.91 percentage points [E37]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash burn ignores the severity of a negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr [E30] and a low cash conversion ratio of 0.51x [E28], which signal a dangerous disconnect between accounting profits and actual cash collection. While the bull attributes borrowings rising to Rs 119 Cr [E32] and a 243.8% surge in work-in-progress [E33] entirely to productive growth spend like the INR170 crore seamless tube project [E74], this aggressive capital expenditure coincides with expanding working capital days from 86.9 to 124 days [E55] and pressures from rising consumable and commodity costs [E84]. Furthermore, the bull's focus on superior return metrics overlooks the fact that foreign and domestic institutions have actively reduced their stakes by 2.56 [E35] and 3.44 percentage points [E36] respectively, suggesting smart money is exiting despite the reported growth. Finally, citing the EV/EBITDA premium as justified by strong TTM sales and profit growth [E11, E16, E19] ignores the warning that price growth has already outpaced profit growth by 19% [E50], leaving expectations dangerously ahead of delivery.
